hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now."
body: A ranked list of 37 ad formats printing right now (AI podcast, report card, iPhone Notes, text on skin, Reddit style, cross-out, fake PDP, tier list, myth vs fact, zero stars…), anchored by a 280-day AI podcast ad. Payload: a Notion doc with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format, plus a 132-ad board.
cta: Notion doc + board links; no comment/follow gate.
idea: Days-active ranked across 37 formats is the honest creative scoreboard; the fake PDP sits among the winners.
sequencing: Receipt: AI podcast at 280 days, longest-running.
Payload: full doc (live ad, days active, brand counts) + 132-ad board.
Method note: found with GetHookd MCP.
formatting: Numbered top-10 teaser + photo + doc links. Curator voice.
why_it_works: The 280-day anchor makes the list feel researched rather than opinionated, and the ungated doc trades funnel for authority.
what_to_steal: The scoreboard habit: rank LC's own formats by days-active and keep the fake-PDP/bundle-picker in the rotation — if it prints for others, it deserves a test cell.

hook: "The statics printing hardest right now don't look like ads at all:"
body: The core thesis post: the statics printing hardest don't look like ads at all — iPhone Notes, iMessage chat, Reddit post, tweet screenshot, email screenshot, app settings screen, breaking news, fake product page. "People scroll past ads. They stop for screenshots." Payload: a 200-ad board + a "Native Statics Machine" doc for making 50 image ads/day.
cta: Board link + doc link; no comment/follow gate.
idea: The screenshot is the thumb-stop: native-UI mimicry (notes, chats, PDPs) earns the stop that polished statics can't.
sequencing: Hook: the hardest-printing statics don't look like ads.
The 8 formats: Notes, iMessage, Reddit, tweet, email, settings, breaking news, fake product page.
Thesis: people scroll past ads; they stop for screenshots.
formatting: Numbered 8-format list + one-line thesis. Minimal, quotable.
why_it_works: One quotable line ("They stop for screenshots") compresses the whole format into a rule, and the production-system doc answers the immediate "how" objection.
what_to_steal: The fake-PDP itself for LC: a screenshot-style static of LC's own product page (reviews, price, "waterproof" badge) run as the ad — plus the 50-statics-a-day production system as the volume target.
